deviations: After a stopping event's popup closes, time resumes at 5 s (as in the original). It is not left paused. Space/P is an explicit pause and keeps that state.
Time is also frozen while the intercept or funding dialog, globe target mode, any queued popup or an OV.Dom modal is open. The original paused in these windows too.
i18n keys use my own prefix (geo.ev.*, geo.toast.*, geo.err.*) instead of the contract's suggested ev.*. This avoids clashes with other areas' files. The dogfight overlay keeps its own df.* keys.
baseDefence result popup: the contract assigns it to CampaignUI, but there is no CampaignUI entry point for it, so GeoUI shows it (with baseAttack before it).

UFOs are named «OVNI-<n>» from their id, matching the dogfight overlay. Type and race appear only when ufo.hyper is set; otherwise size is shown. Place names come from GMath.countryAtMap (presentation outlines, with «Portugal» added in my file) and fall back to the world region, including oceans.
Card actions: «Patrulhar aqui» is shown only for crafts that are out or returning. A transport waiting over a ground target gets «Iniciar missão» (M) instead.
In target mode, clicking a city sends the craft to a point at that city. Clicking the craft's own base orders it home.
Debug-only events (alienBaseBuilt, retaliation) show toasts when ?debug=1 or G.debug is set.
A one-time intro popup «Bem-vindo, Comandante» appears on a new campaign at t = 0, guarded by G.ui.geoIntro.
When G.activeMission blocks the clock while the Geoscape is open, a banner appears with «Cancelar missão» (OV.Campaign.cancelMission), so time can never be stuck forever.
Pinch zoom is continuous (fractional levels, not snapped). +/− and the mouse-wheel notch go to whole levels with animation.
open_issues: Frame rate: rotating at 1440×900 @2× gives 6.7–11 fps in this GPU-less, shared container. JS per moving globe draw is 20–96 ms depending on CPU load, almost all of it inside OV.GlobeRender's direct coarse render plus software rasterising. The ≥ 50 fps target needs checking on a real Mac (Safari and Chrome). Run `node ovni-1999/qa/geo_check.mjs` and read the 'fps a rodar' line.
CampaignUI names its briefing scene 'cbriefing', not the contract's 'briefing' (§6.1). This is harmless for GeoUI, but the contract table should be updated, or that scene renamed.
World never emits interceptOrderInvalid (World engineer's deviation). GeoUI handles it as a toast anyway.
Contract tidy-up for the architect: §6.2 should list the extra GeoUI exports (current, setSpeed, togglePause, select, model). §4 should note that baseDefence/baseAttack popups are shown by GeoUI.
With ?debug=1 the debug toast «Depuração: … base(s) alienígena(s) construída(s)» reveals hidden alien bases. This is intended for testing only.

Gameplay notes seen during QA:
- At month 0, Small Scouts often land under a chasing interceptor, which then waits over the landed UFO with no weapon use.
- The monthly report on an idle January already shows rating «Fraco» from terror sites that were never answered.
- Both match the sim design, but they are worth watching in the pacing bot.

campui.api:
OV.CampaignUI = {
  newGame()                                   push 'newgame' (difficulty → globe placement → name → OV.Campaign.newCampaign → autosave 'auto' → openGeo)
  launchMission(G, siteRef, craftId) → bool    OV.Campaign.startMission (campaign.err.* → pt-PT modal) → push 'cbriefing'
  startBattle(mission, meta) → bool            OV.Battle.create → OV.Game.B → Scenes.replace('battlescape', {B, G, mission, meta, onExit: r => afterBattle(G,B,r), onPlayerTurn: B => Save.save('autoTurn', G, B, {label})})
  afterBattle(G, B, result) → model|null       exactly once per B (WeakSet): finishMission (or abortMission when B has no outcome); removes only victory/gameOver from G.events (the rest stay for GeoUI); autosave 'auto' when outcome 'continue'; replace/push 'cdebrief'; onDone → victory | gameOver | popToGeo
  resume({G, B}) → bool                        B ⇒ Scenes.set('battlescape') with the campaign onExit/onPlayerTurn; ended game ⇒ victory/gameOver; else openGeo(G)
  openGeo(G)                                   OV.GeoUI.open(G) | Scenes.set('geoscape') | Scenes.set('campaignHub') fallback
  popToGeo(G)                                  pops back to the geoscape/campaignHub below, or openGeo
  equip(G, craftId, onDone?)                   push 'equip' (OV.InventoryUI.equipScreen fed by Campaign.equipPool, every change applied with Campaign.applyEquip)
  monthReport(G, report) → Promise             push 'monthReport' overlay; resolves on close; a gameOver/victory call that arrives while it is open waits for «Continuar»
  gameOver(G, reason) ; victory(G)             Scenes.set('gameOver'|'victory')
  baseDefence(G, ev) → Promise                 result modal for a baseDefence event (optional; GeoUI currently shows its own popup)
  saveDialog(G) ; loadDialog()                 push 'saveload' overlay (slots auto/autoTurn/1–3; save/overwrite with confirm, open, export, import, delete, quota offer)
  autosave(G, {silent?}) → {ok, reason?}       slot 'auto' with translated label; quota ⇒ toast «Espaço insuficiente — exporte o jogo» + export offer (once per session)
  saveLabel(G) → «Janeiro 1999 — Base Lusitânia» ; errText(err) → pt-PT text for Error('campaign.err.*'|'save.err.*')
  debug.newgame() → {step, diff, chosen:{lon,lat}, name, view} | null    (QA)
}
Scenes (OV.SceneDefs): newgame {} · cbriefing {G, siteRef, craftId, mission} · equip {G, craftId, onDone?, night?} · cdebrief {G, B, model, loc?, onDone} · monthReport {G, report, onClose?} (isScreen:false) · gameOver {G, reason} · victory {G} · saveload {G?, mode:'save'|'load'} (isScreen:false) · campaignHub {G} (only used while no geoscape scene exists).
screens.js hooks: startBattle(mission, meta) → OV.CampaignUI.startBattle when meta.campaign; resumeGame(st) → OV.CampaignUI.resume when st.G; menu «Nova Campanha» → CampaignUI.newGame(), «Carregar» → CampaignUI.loadDialog(), new entry {id:'ufopaedia', key:'up.menu', act: () => OV.Ufopaedia.open(null)}; OV.Screens.ui = {makeScreen, header, panelSection, seg, goBack, portraitEl, itemIconEl, unitSpriteEl, canvasCopy} exported for reuse.
battle_ui.js hook: battlescape params gain onPlayerTurn(B), called after beginBattle and after every endPlayerTurn when the turn is back to X-COM (no-op for quick battles).
campui.summary:
The campaign flow screens are done and verified end to end. qa/campaign_flow_check.mjs passes 113 of 113 checks with no console errors and no missing i18n keys. The Node suite passes with --strict (563 of 563). battle_play.mjs and full_battle.mjs pass. screens_check.mjs fails one check only: it counts 7 menu entries, and the Ufopédia entry you asked for makes 8 (one-line fix in open_issues).

**What the player gets:**
- **New campaign:** difficulty cards (Recruta, Veterano, Super-humano), each with one line plus alien accuracy, crew size and the council limit (−900, −700, −500). Keys 1–3, optional seed, last choice remembered.
- **Base placement:** then the globe in placeBase mode, pre-centred on Lisbon, with Lisbon already chosen. Land only (sea clicks are refused with a toast). Trackpad drag and two-finger scroll rotate, pinch or ctrl+wheel zoom, double-click centres. The side panel shows coordinates, region, map country, a warning when the site is outside the funding countries, and which funding countries the radar circle covers.
- **Base name:** «Base Lusitânia» in Portugal, otherwise «Base <região>», updated live until the player types a name. «Fundar base» creates the campaign, autosaves and opens the Geoscape.
- **Briefing:** same look as the quick-battle briefing. Title by mission kind, place (city, country, region), terrain, time of day, craft, difficulty, objectives, race (or «Desconhecida» with a hyper-wave hint) and crew estimate.
- **Briefing warnings:** missing template items, no Medi-Kit, night mission without flares, overloaded soldiers, empty seats.
- **Briefing keys:** E «Equipar», Enter «Iniciar missão», Esc «Cancelar» (calls cancelMission).
- **Equip:** the inventory equipScreen in its own scene. Tab and 1–9 switch soldier, Esc cancels a pick or closes.
- **Battle:** autosave to the autoTurn slot at the start of every player turn. finishMission or abortMission runs exactly once.
- **Campaign mission report:** score lines with item icons, mission rating, which region got the points, aliens killed or captured, containment results (stored or lost), memorial, wound days, items delivered to the base stores, lost equipment, storage over-capacity warning, stat gains and promotions. Then back to the Geoscape that was left below, or to the victory or game-over screen.
- **Monthly report:**
  - rating label and colour, the council message (the council.* texts are defined), a score breakdown with bars;
  - a per-region table, shown only once Economy adds per-region data to the report (patch in open_issues; today it does not appear in a real game);
  - funding per country with arrows, amounts and pact tags, income against each upkeep line;
  - warnings for debt, a second bad month, new pacts, a base revealed by agents and defeat.
- **End screens:** game over with a title and text for each reason (council, debt, base lost, Cydonia), campaign statistics and the memorial, with «Carregar» and «Menu principal». Victory has a gold banner with light rays, a short epilogue, the squad that won, statistics and a memorial.
- **Save/load dialog:** slots auto, autoTurn and 1–3 with label, game date, funds, difficulty, battle tag, real save time and corrupt state. Save or overwrite (with confirmation), open, delete, export a slot, export the current game, import a file. Every save.err and write reason has a pt-PT text. The quota error shows the toast and offers an export.
- **Everywhere:** all buttons have tooltips with their shortcut, sounds go through OV.audio, and touch targets are at least 32 px.

**QA:** three rounds of reviewing screenshots at 1440×900 and 1024×700 led to fixes. Canvas clicks were blocked by `#hud > *`. Some panels shrank. The briefing soldier cards, the equip header and the battle-save labels were cramped at 1024. The main-menu hub panel was in the wrong place.

The QA script also has a `--stub-geo` flag that serves an empty geo_ui.js, so the flow can be tested apart from that file. I also ran it against the current geo_ui.js: it integrates (welcome popup, month report over the globe). That run's one failure was a check that compared the date exactly while the real clock kept running; it now allows a small margin.

Screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-HelloWorld/b8cfbac1-629a-5f58-8dfb-0f752cc84b7c/scratchpad/ui4/campaign/ and, for the run with the real Geoscape, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-HelloWorld/b8cfbac1-629a-5f58-8dfb-0f752cc84b7c/scratchpad/ui4/campaign-geo/.
deviations: Campaign briefing and debrief are their own scenes, 'cbriefing' and 'cdebrief'. They reuse the .scr-brief/.scr-deb look and the helpers exported from screens.js. The contract named the shared 'briefing'/'debrief' scenes, but those cannot do the «Equipar» step, cancelMission on Esc, containment results, wound days, the delivered-to-stores list or the storage warning. If someone pushes screens.js 'briefing' with meta.campaign, «Iniciar missão» still goes through CampaignUI.startBattle through the new hook.

After «Equipar» changes something, the briefing calls cancelMission then startMission again, so the shown mission (squad, craft items) is exact. This draws one more u32 from the map stream for each briefing whose equipment changed. It is deterministic for the same UI actions.

afterBattle removes only the victory/gameOver events from G.events, which it handles through model.outcome. Other events from finishMission (e.g. craftLost) stay queued, so GeoUI shows them after its next World.step. The contract says CampaignUI drains after its call.

Extra scenes and entry points beyond §6: 'campaignHub' (used only while no geoscape scene exists), CampaignUI.baseDefence(G, ev), popToGeo, equip, saveLabel, errText, debug.newgame(). Battle autosave labels are «OVNI Despenhado · turno N»; geoscape labels are «Janeiro 1999 — Base Lusitânia».
The monthly report draws a per-region X-COM vs alien table only when report.regions exists. Economy.monthEnd does not provide it yet (patch in open_issues).

Briefing and debrief fall back to the real-outline country (GMath.countryAtMap, presentation only) when the site is not in a funding country, e.g. «Portugal · Europa». I added country.portugal to my i18n file for this.
open_issues: qa/screens_check.mjs (not mine) now fails one check: 'menu: 7 entradas'. The Ufopédia entry you asked for makes 8. One-line patch at line 72: `check((await page.locator('.scr-menu .scr-mi').count()) === 8, 'menu: 8 entradas');`. Its other 48 checks pass, including the newgame scene and Esc. The arrow-key order quick → load → new is unchanged.

Economy patch for the per-region monthly score (js/sim/geo/economy.js, monthEnd, before `const report = {`): `const regions = {}; for (const id of Object.keys(m.xcom.regions).concat(Object.keys(m.alien.regions))) regions[id] = { xcom: m.xcom.regions[id] | 0, alien: m.alien.regions[id] | 0 };` then add `regions,` to the report literal. CampaignUI.monthReport already renders a «Por região» table from report.regions (shape {regionId:{xcom, alien}}); QA fakes this field. It must be read before score.month is reset, which happens after the report is built.

GeoUI integration: GeoUI calls launchMission/monthReport/gameOver/victory/saveDialog/autosave, all of which exist. It shows its own baseDefence popup; CampaignUI.baseDefence(G, ev) is available if they prefer the more detailed modal. My first run against geo_ui.js hit a TypeError in its refreshTime (geo_ui.js:636, 'setting title'). The latest run against the real geo_ui.js has no console errors.

Contract tidy-up for the architect (§6.1/§6.2): add the scenes 'cbriefing', 'cdebrief' and 'campaignHub', the battlescape param onPlayerTurn(B), the entry points CampaignUI.equip/popToGeo/baseDefence/errText/saveLabel, and OV.Screens.ui (shared screen helpers).
BaseUI can open the contract's 'equip' scene with {G, craftId, onDone}. Craft in the hangar ⇒ the base stores are offered; away ⇒ only the craft's equipment.
